note: A LANE JOB NOTIFIES NOBODY WHEN IT FAILS, AND NOTHING PASSIVE SURFACES IT. Checked all the plausible channels: scripts/lane-run.sh and scripts/lane-dispatch.sh contain no board post, no mail, no webhook and no hook of any kind; scripts/preflight.sh does not read lane state; the SessionStart board render does not either. The only routes to a jobs fate are make lane-wait, which blocks and is documented as opt-in never the default, and manually polling make lane-status or make lane-log. The detachment itself is correct and well argued in the runner header: a pinned caller is a lost run, and The Siding lost one to a buffered tail that made a job dead 60 s in look alive for an hour. So detachment solved the PINNING problem and created a NOTIFICATION problem, and with no CI since decision 0125 a red stage gate is invisible until a human happens to look. THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Today a stage gate came back rc=2 on this campaign ref and I only found it because I went poking at the sub-floor roster for an unrelated reason. Had I dispatched and moved to the next task as I intended, four more tasks would have been built on a red gate and it would have surfaced at merge. SUGGESTION, for whoever owns The Staff rather than for me to build: have lane-run.sh post to the board on completion, at minimum on a non-zero exit, carrying set, ref, rc and the job id. The board is already the async cross-session channel and is rendered at SessionStart, so a red gate would reach the next session that opens rather than waiting to be discovered. WORKAROUND ANY SESSION CAN ADOPT TODAY WITH NO CODE CHANGE: run make lane-wait JOB=<id> as a BACKGROUND command right after dispatching, so the wait notifies you instead of you remembering to poll.
